answer: On a clear cold night the temperature near the ground falls below the air a few metres up, and the claimant reports both readings at the coldest hour of the night. A comet of frost forms in the valley while a voyage of cold air drains downhill, and the atlas of local stations confirms which hollows freeze first. Faking the pattern needs a real thermometer at each elevation, because a copied pair of numbers cannot reproduce the way real inversions deepen hour by hour.
